早期版本為裝在低音鼓邊的小鈸，後有鉸接板端裝小鈸的裝置，再演變為踏板驅動的低鈸架: Early versions were small cymbals mounted on the rim of the bass drum; there followed a device with a small cymbal on the end of a hinged board, and that in turn became the pedal-driven low stand. Around 1926 Barney Walberg built a hi-hat playable with hand and foot. Papa Jo Jones is regarded as the first recognised master, and the rhythm he struck as the cymbals opened and closed drove the development of the ride cymbal. From the late 1960s the standard was mostly 14 inches; in the 1970s hard rock moved to 15 inches; the 1980s brought small cymbals of 12 and 10 inches, and the 1990s 8-inch mini hi-hats; after that the standard returned to 14 and 13 inches, and the X-hat and remote-control units were developed.

踩鈸以腳與鼓棒操作。初學先將腳放於踏板，踩下使上鈸貼合下鈸，練習短促悶音；再以鼓: The hi-hat is worked with the foot and with drumsticks. A beginner first rests the foot on the pedal and presses down so that the top cymbal meets the bottom one, practising the short closed sound; then strikes the closed pair with a stick and tries the open sound, opening after closing, closing after opening and the other states. A right-handed drummer usually works the pedal with the left foot and may use one or two sticks; the traditional groove has the right hand on the hi-hat and the left on the snare, though the left hand can take the hi-hat instead. The point of the practice is a steady opening and closing, control of foot pressure and of striking force, so that everything from a soft accompaniment to an accented crescendo comes out clearly.

踩鈸是標準鼓組中的體鳴樂器，常見於搖滾、流行、爵士與藍調等北美流行音樂場合。它可: The hi-hat is an idiophone of the standard drum kit, common in North American popular music settings such as rock, pop, jazz and blues. Pressed shut with the foot pedal it gives a short closed sound, and struck with a stick in its open or closed state it produces the soft accompaniment before a folk tune or a guitar solo, or the loud drive of heavy metal. In jazz the foot often opens and closes the pedal, stressing the second and fourth beats; in hip-hop it appears as an eighth-note pattern and is often triggered from a drum machine or sampler. In a kit with two bass drums a drop clutch keeps it closed for playing.
踩鈸音色明亮尖銳，具有典型的金屬質感。當踏板踩下時，兩片鈸閉合發出清脆的「嗤」聲: The hi-hat's timbre is bright and sharp, with the classic metallic quality. When the pedal is pressed the two cymbals close and give a crisp tssh; the sound sits in the instrument's high frequency range and carries well. Releasing the pedal separates the cymbals and produces a more open sound with a longer resonance, richer and more complex in timbre. Its resonance is unusual: closed, the sound is short and tight; open, it produces a sustained metallic shimmer. Against the thick, low sound of the drumheads the hi-hat's high frequencies stand in sharp contrast; unlike the deep resonance of a gong it is lighter and more agile. As the timekeeping foundation of the kit it supplies a steady, strongly rhythmic texture.
踩鈸（Hi-hat cymbal）是體鳴樂器，由一對小型至中型鈸、腳踏板與金屬支: The hi-hat cymbal is an idiophone made of a pair of small to medium cymbals, a foot pedal and a metal stand, common in North American drum kits. The bottom cymbal is fixed and the top one is mounted on a rod, so that pressing the pedal brings the top cymbal down onto the bottom one; the player controls the opening with the foot and also strikes the cymbals with sticks, producing a short closed sound, a continuing shimmer or changes of loud and soft. It is used mainly by drummers in rock, pop, jazz and blues.
